name: HivePunk 547
subject: Hugging Face Hub dataset publishing (huggingface_hub)
thesis: Publishing is straightforward in the official docs — create repo, upload files, add README.md card — but file-size/LFS and token-permission pitfalls mean a publishable dataset needs verified files, a complete card, and official-doc confirmation of the huggingface_hub route before claiming it is ready.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The Hugging Face Hub hosts over 3M models, 1M datasets, and 2M AI apps (Spaces).
claims.quote: The Hugging Face Hub is the reference AI platform for open ML. It hosts over 3M models, 1M datasets, and 2M AI apps (Spaces), all open and publicly available.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: To create a dataset repository via the UI, click the profile and select New Dataset, pick a name, and choose public or private.
claims.quote: Click on your profile and select New Dataset to create a new dataset repository . Pick a name for your dataset, and choose whether it is a public or private dataset.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: After creating a repository, upload via the Files and versions tab using Add file.
claims.quote: Once you’ve created a repository, navigate to the Files and versions tab to add a file. Select Add file to upload your dataset files.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The Create Dataset Card button creates a README.md file in the repository, with Metadata UI fields such as license, language, and task categories at the top.
claims.quote: Click on Create Dataset Card to create a Dataset card . This button creates a README.md file in your repository. At the top, you’ll see the Metadata UI with several fields to select from such as license, language, and task categories.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The huggingface_hub library allows managing repositories, including creating repos and uploading datasets to the Hub.
claims.quote: The rich features set in the huggingface_hub library allows you to manage repositories, including creating repos and uploading datasets to the Hub.

risks: Text files over 10MB not tracked by Git LFS by default will not be committed and uploaded, per Datasets docs.
Git route needs Git LFS and, per third-party memo, a token with read and write permissions.
Third-party Zenn article states it is AI-translated, experimental, and may contain errors, so its code examples need official verification.
Dataset card value depends on correct metadata; pages call license, language, and task categories the most important tags for discovery.
Public vs private choice is made at repository creation; pages describe public as visible to anyone.
